title: "Module 6 --- Flapping simulation (Ptera)"
---

## Summary

The wing and tail geometry are chosen here. Candidate geometries are simulated in Ptera. Modules 7 and 8 build whatever is decided here.

## Requirements

|           |                             |
|-----------|-----------------------------|
| **Bring** | Laptop with Ptera installed |
| **Read**  | This page                   |

## Deliverable

A wing planform and a tail geometry, with the simulation output that justifies them, carried forward into [Module 7](07-wings.qmd) and [Module 8](08-tail-housing.qmd).

::: callout-important
## To be written by the instructor

This module has **no counterpart in the manufacturing guide** --- the guide documents the research robot's final geometry, not the design exercise. The following need to be written from course material:

- Ptera installation and a worked example
- The provided motor power curve, and its format
- What "most efficient thrust profile" means quantitatively here, and how it is scored
- Constraints the students must respect so their geometry remains buildable with the frame from [Module 5](05-frame-crank.qmd) --- span limits, root fitting, mass budget
- Whether teams may deviate from the reference wing, and by how much
:::

::: callout-note
## Checkpoint

A geometry chosen, with simulation evidence, and confirmed buildable against the frame and wing-root hardware.
:::
